questions.text: How long have you been experiencing fatigue, and would you describe it as tiredness after exertion or persistent exhaustion even at rest?
questions.purpose: Characterise duration and pattern to distinguish physiological tiredness from pathological fatigue
options: Less than 2 weeks, related to exertion or poor sleep
More than 6 weeks, persistent despite adequate rest

questions.text: Have you noticed pallor, breathlessness on mild exertion, or racing heartbeat — which could indicate anaemia?
questions.purpose: Features of anaemia require urgent full blood count

questions.text: Do you have unexplained weight loss, night sweats, persistent fever, or new lumps alongside the fatigue?
questions.purpose: Constitutional symptoms with fatigue raise concern for malignancy or serious systemic disease

questions.text: Are you experiencing low mood, loss of interest in activities, sleep disturbance, or poor concentration?
questions.purpose: Depression and anxiety are the most common reversible causes of persistent fatigue

questions.text: Do you have symptoms of hypothyroidism — weight gain, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, or hair loss?
questions.purpose: Hypothyroidism is a common reversible endocrine cause of fatigue

questions.text: Do you have known diabetes or symptoms of uncontrolled blood sugar — excessive thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision?
questions.purpose: Hyperglycaemia and diabetes are metabolic causes of persistent fatigue

questions.text: Has the fatigue been present for more than 6 months and significantly limits your daily activities despite rest?
questions.purpose: Disabling fatigue >6 months affecting function may meet criteria for chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS/ME) workup
